chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to one thousand dirhams and one dirham for one thousand dirhams, and two dinars, if two dinars or less or more enter into it, then there is no objection to it."

key_terms.دَخَلَ فِيهَا: Enter into it (referring to the inclusion of a specific amount)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging unequal amounts of gold or silver coins in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the condition for permissible unequal exchange (tafaddul) of the same currency type is clarified as the inclusion of at least two dinars (or equivalent dirham weight) within the total transaction value, thereby distinguishing it from riba al-fadl. This ruling, recorded in al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the scholarly consensus that small discrepancies in weight or count are tolerated to facilitate daily trade, provided the threshold of 'two dinars' is met to ensure the exchange is not merely a disguised loan with interest.
